evals.prompt: I want to build a SaaS that helps small restaurants manage table reservations and customer preferences. Target market is independent restaurants with 2-5 dining rooms. Users should get SMS reminders 1 hour before their reservation, and we'll charge restaurants $49/month.
evals.expected_output: PRD must contain all 10 sections from SKILL.md. Problem Statement identifies target (small independent restaurants) and pain point (no-show management, preference tracking). Success Criteria must include measurable outcomes with numbers: e.g., '90% uptime SLA', 'reduce restaurant no-shows by 25%', 'support 500+ concurrent reservations/month'. Functional Requirements must be numbered (FR-01, FR-02, etc.), use RFC 2119 language (MUST/SHOULD/MAY), and each must have testable acceptance criteria with measurable thresholds (NOT adjectives). Example: 'FR-03: System MUST send SMS reminder exactly 60 minutes before reservation. Acceptance: SMS delivery within 1 minute of scheduled time.' Technical Requirements must specify stack choices (e.g., Next.js, Node.js backend, Supabase database). Service Manifest must name exact services: Stripe (payments), Twilio (SMS), Supabase (database), SendGrid or similar (email). Data Model must show key entities (restaurant, table, reservation, customer, preference) and relationships. User Flows section must describe primary happy paths (restaurant manager setup, customer booking, reminder delivery) plus error states. Risks & Open Questions must include likelihood (high/medium/low) and mitigation strategies. Scope Boundaries must explicitly list 3+ things NOT in v1 (e.g., 'No walk-in management', 'No staff scheduling', 'No kitchen display integration'). PRD should NOT contain vague language like 'fast', 'user-friendly', or 'seamless' without measurable criteria. PRD should NOT skip any of the 10 sections.

evals.prompt: hey so i wanna make a mobile app 4 tracking ur moods throughout the day?? like u just tap in how ur feeling and it shows trends over time. kinda like an emotional journal but rly simple and minimal design lol. maybe monetize w/ premium features later
evals.expected_output: Despite highly informal input register (lowercase, typos, slang, vague 'later' monetization), output PRD must be rigorous and complete with all 10 sections. Skill must extract core idea: daily mood logging with trend visualization. Problem Statement should identify target user (people wanting to understand their emotional patterns) and pain (existing emotion tracking apps are too complex/feature-bloated). Success Criteria must quantify: e.g., '80% of active users log mood 5+ days/week', 'trend detection accuracy >= 90% on rolling 7-day windows', 'app startup time <2s'. Functional Requirements (FR-01, FR-02, etc.) must include: mood logging (with acceptance: 'save mood entry within 500ms'), trend visualization (with acceptance: 'display chart for last 30 days within 1s'), possibly data export. Each acceptance criterion must be measurable. Technical Requirements should identify appropriate stack given 'simple' intent (e.g., React Native or Flutter frontend, Firebase Realtime Database or PostgreSQL backend, NOT over-engineered). Service Manifest must list actual services: Firebase (or Supabase), analytics (optional but address whether included), payment processor if monetized (Stripe or RevenueCat). Data Model must define: mood_entries table (user_id, timestamp, mood_value, notes), mood_trends (computed or stored), user profiles. User Flows must cover: daily logging flow, trend viewing flow, settings flow, data deletion flow (GDPR/privacy). Risks section MUST address: user privacy with mental health data (high-severity), habit formation for retention, data deletion compliance (GDPR), data breach sensitivity. Scope Boundaries must explicitly define premium vs. v1 scope: e.g., 'NOT in v1: mood sharing, doctor integration, wearable sync, notifications, custom themes (premium feature requires definition of what IS premium)'. PRD should NOT hallucinate unneeded complexity. Should NOT leave monetization undefined (must specify what 'premium' means).

evals.prompt: /idea I have an idea for a new feature. We already have a Next.js SaaS app for expense tracking with Supabase backend and Stripe integration. We want to add group expense splitting and automatic settlement. Users should be able to split an expense across multiple people and Stripe should handle the payments between them.
evals.expected_output: PRD must recognize this is a feature addition to an existing codebase, not a greenfield project. Problem Statement should reference existing user base and note that users want to split group expenses (e.g., shared meals, trips) without manual calculation. Success Criteria should be feature-specific: e.g., 'settlement calculates minimum payment transfers using graph algorithm', 'all splits within a group reconcile in under 5 seconds', '100% accuracy of money owed calculations', 'support groups of up to 20 members'. Technical Requirements must respect existing architecture (Next.js, Supabase, Stripe) and specify only new additions: new Stripe webhook routes for settlement, database schema for splits (split_groups table, split_ledger table, settlement_transaction table), payment logic for inter-user transfers. Service Manifest: Stripe (existing, new settlement webhook routes), Supabase (new schema), no new external services required if using Stripe transfers. Data Model must show: split_groups (group_id, members[], total_amount, payer), split_ledger (who_owes_who, amount), settlement_transactions (from_user, to_user, amount, status, stripe_transfer_id). User Flows must include: create group, add expense to group, view split breakdown, initiate settlement, confirm payment. Functional Requirements must handle: FR-01 'System MUST calculate minimum payment transfers from all-owe-all, acceptance: uses linear-time algorithm for n members, produces optimal solution', FR-02 'System MUST initiate Stripe transfer between group members, acceptance: transfer initiates within 1 second of settlement click, webhook confirms transfer status'. Risks must address: payment failure recovery (what if Stripe transfer fails mid-group settlement), concurrent splits (race condition if two users add expense simultaneously), partial group payment (some members pay, others don't). Scope Boundaries: 'NOT in v1: multi-currency splits, recurring group expenses, group invitations via email, settlement notifications via SMS'. PRD should NOT suggest Supabase migration or Stripe architectural changes. Should NOT treat this as greenfield (should reference existing codebase).

This intentionally ambiguous one-liner must trigger rigorous questioning, not hallucination. Phase 1 (Explore) will identify ambiguities in the idea. Phase 2 (Requirements Extraction) should either: (A) produce a PRD that acknowledges missing scope definition and extensively lists blocking questions under Risks & Open Questions section (e.g., 'OPEN: What is target user demographic? College students, professionals, general public?', 'OPEN: Real-time messaging or async posts?', 'OPEN: Mobile-first, web, or both?', 'OPEN: Monetization model or free?'), OR (B) produce a minimal PRD that Phase 3 (Review) will reject as insufficiently specified. If option B occurs, Phase 3 should return REVISE verdict with blocking_issues listing: 'Problem Statement too vague — two engineers would build different products', 'Target user undefined', 'Success Criteria unmeasurable'. Then Phase 2 re-runs to incorporate feedback. After max 3 revision cycles, if still ambiguous, PRD should gracefully escalate to human for clarification. Output should NOT be a hallucinated 10-page PRD with architectural decisions made without user input (e.g., should NOT assume PostgreSQL + Redis + React without asking). Output should NOT skip target user definition or success criteria. If PRD is produced, it must have explicit 'OPEN QUESTIONS' section with 5+ blocking questions listed for human to resolve before building.
